# Development

This is built on top of Webman, a high performance HTTP Service Framework for PHP based on [Workerman](https://github.com/walkor/workerman).

## API Specification

We are utilizing the OpenAPI 3 (formerly known as Swagger) spec for this API.  It is basically the next evolution of SOAP API's with well defined functions, parameters, and responses.  While there are many editors out there I'm currently using SwaggerHub to do most of the editing of the spec.

## Webman Framework

After testing *every* PHP library out there dealing with concurrent/asynchronous processing many times over the years I've found [Workerman](https://github.com/walkor/workerman) to be the overall best.  It has proven more stable and by far faster than the alternatives with the one big downside being that its documentation and code comments are all in Chinese.  [Webman](https://github.com/walkor/webman) is a fairly recently created web framework on top of [Workerman](https://github.com/walkor/workerman).  There had been many previously created frameworks based on workerman and while some were good Webman seemed to hit that perfect balance between ease-of-use and power.

The Chinese documentation is easily readable Using either the auto translate in Chrome or an addon like [Translate Web Pages](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/traduzir-paginas-web/) for Firefox.

# Caliber Learnings

Source: https://github.com/interserver/mailbaby-mail-api/blob/master/CALIBER_LEARNINGS.md

# Caliber Learnings

Accumulated patterns and anti-patterns from development sessions.
Auto-managed by [caliber](https://github.com/caliber-ai-org/ai-setup) — do not edit manually.

- **[convention]** Agent-readiness scanners check several conflicting/overlapping well-known paths for the MCP server card. This project serves the SAME card JSON at all of: `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` (canonical SEP-1649), `/.well-known/mcp.json` (SEP-1960 alias), `/.well-known/mcp` (extension-less alias), and `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` (legacy). Add new aliases as routes in `config/route.php` pointing at `Mcp::serverCard` rather than duplicating the body.
- **[convention]** Agent Skills 0.2.0 (`agentskills.io`) requires SKILL.md frontmatter with `name` (max 64 chars, lowercase + digits + hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen) and `description` (max 1024 chars, non-empty). Skills live in `app/Mcp/Skills/<slug>.md` and are advertised via `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json` whose `skills[].digest` field is a `sha256:` hash of the file. Don't put skills under `public/` — they're served by `Mcp::agentSkill` so the routing/digest stays consistent with the index.
- **[gotcha]** WebMCP manifest format is officially `TBD` per the upstream proposal at `webmachinelearning/webmcp` — the well-known path is not formally specified. Current scanners look for `mcpServers` + `tools` at `/.well-known/webmcp` (no extension) or `/.well-known/webmcp.json`. Serve both URLs and include both the proposal's hinted `tools[].{name,description,inputSchema}` shape AND an `mcpServers` block with `{type:'streamable-http',url,headers:{X-API-KEY:'${MAILBABY_API_KEY}'}}` so existing readers all match.
- **[gotcha]** The WebMCP check on isitagentready.com is a JavaScript-RUNTIME check, not a static-manifest check: the scanner loads the homepage and looks for code calling `navigator.modelContext.registerTool(...)`. Serving a JSON manifest at `/.well-known/webmcp{,.json}` (the upstream `TBD` declarative-discovery proposal shape with `mcpServers`/`tools`) is necessary but NOT sufficient — you also need a `<script>` on the homepage that registers tools at runtime. This project's runtime side is `public/webmcp.js`, loaded with `<script src="/webmcp.js" defer>` from `public/index.html`.
- **[gotcha]** Don't try to functionally smoke-test `public/webmcp.js` by stubbing `global.navigator.modelContext = ...` in Node — Node 20+ already exposes a built-in read-only `navigator` global, so the assignment silently no-ops and your IIFE bails out at the `'modelContext' in navigator` guard with `Registered tools: 0`. Use `Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'modelContext', { value: stub, configurable: true })` instead. Same trap will hit any future browser-API smoke test in this repo.
- **[pattern]** When mirroring an OpenAPI spec into JS-side tool definitions (e.g. `public/webmcp.js`), keep the description-truncation rule identical to the server-side parser (this project: 900-char sentence-aware cutoff falling back to a hard 897-char slice). Otherwise WebMCP and `/mcp` will advertise differently-worded tool descriptions for the same operation, which agents notice.
- **[env]** To use `gh` CLI on this host you must `unset GITHUB_TOKEN` first — the env var (if set) overrides keyring auth and may point at a different identity/scope than the user wants. Run `unset GITHUB_TOKEN && gh auth status` before any `gh pr`/`gh repo`/`gh api` work.
- **[gotcha]** The PHPMailer-Async-Proxy-Workerman fork lives as a nested git repo at `PHPMailer-Async-Proxy-Workerman/` inside the parent `mailbaby-mail-api` working tree, with its own `.git/`. It is `.gitignore`d in the parent (alongside `.opencode/`). Do not `git add PHPMailer-Async-Proxy-Workerman/` from the parent repo — work inside the nested dir for fork changes, and consume it from the parent via Composer (`detain/phpmailer-async-proxy-workerman` with a `repositories[].vcs` entry in `composer.json`).
- **[pattern]** When swapping a Composer dep to a forked package, add a `"repositories": [{"type": "vcs", "url": "https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git"}]` block AND rename the required package, then run `composer update <new-name>` (NOT `composer install` or `composer require` — `update` is what re-resolves with the new VCS source). Verify the swap with `php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; echo (new ReflectionClass("PHPMailer\\PHPMailer\\PHPMailer"))->getConstant("VERSION");'` before running tests.
- **[gotcha]** PHPMailer 7.0.2's `src/SMTP.php` has blocking I/O at fixed line numbers: `stream_socket_client` (line 423), `fsockopen` fallback (440), `stream_set_timeout` (475, 1348), `stream_socket_enable_crypto` (508, STARTTLS), `fclose` (767), `fwrite` (1255, `client_send`), `stream_select`/`fgets`/`feof` in `get_lines()` (1354-1413). Anywhere stock PHPMailer is called inside a Workerman worker, it stalls the entire event-loop process for the SMTP round-trip — use the async fork (`detain/phpmailer-async-proxy-workerman`) or push the send to a background worker.
- **[convention]** Author identity for this project's commits is `Joe Huss <detain@interserver.net>`. The user occasionally typos it as `detain@intertserver.net` (extra `t`) in chat — always normalize to `interserver.net` before committing. Both `mailbaby-mail-api/composer.json` and `.git/config` are authoritative.
- **[fix]** `gh pr create` failing with `GraphQL: Head sha can't be blank, Base sha can't be blank, No commits between master and <branch>, Head ref must be a branch (createPullRequest)` even when `git log origin/master..HEAD` clearly shows commits is almost always a missing/wrong default-repo binding (not a real "no commits" problem). Run `gh repo set-default interserver/mailbaby-mail-api` first, then retry — the error message is misleading.
- **[gotcha]** When using the async PHPMailer fork's `PHPMailer::setSMTPInstance()` to swap in a custom SMTP (e.g. one with `WorkermanTransport` attached), it REPLACES the previous SMTP instance — any PROXY-protocol builder previously installed via `setProxyProtocol()` is dropped with it. Call `setSMTPInstance()` (or any helper that wraps it, like `attachAsyncTransport()`) BEFORE `setProxyProtocol(Configurator::v1(...))`, never after. Verify with `$mailer->getSMTPInstance()->getProxyProtocolBuilder() !== null` before sending.
- **[pattern]** To smoke-test the async-fork PHPMailer wiring without a real SMTP target, run a one-liner `php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; ...'` that (a) builds a PHPMailer, (b) attaches `WorkermanTransport`, (c) calls `setProxyProtocol(Configurator::v1(...))`, then asserts `getSMTPInstance()->getProxyProtocolBuilder() !== null` and `get_class($smtp->getTransport()) === WorkermanTransport::class`. Catches namespace-import typos and the setSMTPInstance-ordering trap before the next `php vendor/bin/phpunit` run.
- **[gotcha]** `PHPMailer\PHPMailer\ProxyProtocol\Configurator::v1($srcIp, $dstIp, ...)` synchronously validates that src and dst are the same family (both IPv4 or both IPv6). An IPv6 API client paired with `mail.api_server_ip` set to IPv4 (or the auto-detected IPv4) throws `ProxyProtocol\Exception` and escapes the controller as an uncaught 500. Wrap the call in try/catch and fall back to `Configurator::v1Unknown()` (emits `PROXY UNKNOWN\r\n`, which any compliant PROXY receiver must accept) so the send still completes.
- **[convention]** SMTP connection pooling and PROXY-protocol v1 are mutually exclusive in this project. A PROXY-pinned connection advertises a specific peer-IP at TCP connect time, so reusing it for a different client would silently misreport the source IP. `app/controller/Mail.php` hard-disables the pool whenever `mail.proxy_protocol_enabled` is true — never flip both flags on at once. When PROXY is on, every send must open a fresh connection (current production path).
- **[pattern]** When the async PHPMailer fork is available, attach the SMTP transport via `PHPMailer\PHPMailer\Async\TransportFactory::auto()` rather than instantiating `WorkermanTransport`/`WorkermanConnectionTransport` directly. The factory picks the right backend for the current host (Workerman worker → connection-based, Revolt available → stream-based, neither → stock blocking) so the same call site works in CLI, PHPUnit, and the live worker.
- **[pattern]** Webman worker-local resource pools (SMTP, DB, etc.) belong as `static` properties on the controller class so they survive across requests inside a single worker process. Each of the 16 workers gets its OWN independent pool — that's intentional, not a bug; sizes like `pool_max_per_key` are per-worker.
- **[gotcha]** `WorkermanConnectionTransport` guards `write/readLine` with an in-fiber check that throws when called outside a fiber. This means pool `release()` (internally `reset()` + stash) and explicit `$smtp->quit(true)` MUST happen INSIDE the same `FiberRunner::run()` closure that did the send — not after it returns. Calling them post-Fiber also re-enters a fresh private Revolt loop that doesn't track the long-lived `AsyncTcpConnection` watchers, causing hangs. Pattern in `app/controller/Mail.php::rawsend()`: do MAIL/RCPT/DATA, then either `pool->release()` or `quit(true)` on the same fiber, then return only a plain array of results to the outer scope.
- **[gotcha]** Webman's `config/server.php` defaults `event_loop` to `''`, which lands on Workerman's `Select` driver. The async SMTP transport in this project (`WorkermanTransport`/`WorkermanConnectionTransport` + `FiberRunner`) only stays non-blocking when the worker loop and the SMTP loop are the SAME loop — pin `event_loop` to `\Workerman\Events\Fiber::class` (Revolt-backed). Otherwise `FiberRunner::run()` spins up a private Revolt loop per call and the worker's HTTP loop stalls during SMTP I/O. `test/Unit/WorkerEventLoopTest.php` asserts this — keep the test green.
- **[pattern]** To register `onWorkerStart`/`onWorkerStop` hooks in Webman, create a class implementing `Webman\Bootstrap` (single `public static function start(?Worker $worker)`) and add it to `config/bootstrap.php` alongside `support\bootstrap\Session`. To chain onto an existing handler instead of clobbering it, capture `$prev = $worker->onWorkerStop` and call `$prev($w)` after your own logic. Example: `app/bootstrap/SmtpPoolBootstrap.php` drains the SMTP pool on worker stop.
- **[pattern]** Quick smoke-boot the webman server WITHOUT leaving a process behind: `timeout 3 php start.php start 2>&1 | tail -30 &; sleep 1; curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:8787/; wait 2>/dev/null`. Catches config-load errors (bad `event_loop` class, broken bootstrap registration) without needing to manually kill the server. Pair with the in-process `php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; require "support/helpers.php"; $config = require "config/server.php"; ...'` check — note that `config/server.php` uses `env()` which only resolves after `support/helpers.php` is loaded.
- **[correction]** **Do NOT run `php start.php` (or restart webman) on this host** — production runs on a different machine. There may be a long-lived local webman process visible via `pgrep -f 'php start.php'` (e.g. PID 2557867) but it is NOT what serves api.mailbaby.net. Verify deployed changes by curling `https://api.mailbaby.net/...` after the user pushes, not by starting webman locally. Live-boot smoke tests with `php start.php start &` followed by `pkill -f 'start.php start'` consistently hang the Bash tool out to timeout on this host — prefer the in-process `php -r 'require "vendor/autoload.php"; require "support/helpers.php"; $config = require "config/server.php"; ...'` sanity check, which exercises the same config-load path without binding the port.
- **[gotcha]** Composer's `version` field schema regex rejects any pre-release suffix that isn't dot- or hyphen-separated, e.g. `8.0.0-async.0` is REJECTED (`Does not match the regex pattern ^[vV]?\d+(?:[.-]\d+){0,3}[._-]...`). Valid alternatives include `8.0.0-alpha2`, `8.0.0+async.0`, or `8.0.0-alpha.2+async`. When picking a custom suffix scheme for an in-house fork, run `composer validate --no-check-publish` against the candidate first — VCS-installed packages (e.g. `detain/phpmailer-async-proxy-workerman` installed via `repositories[].vcs`) report as `dev-master` in `vendor/composer/installed.json` regardless of the declared `version` string.
- **[gotcha]** `composer.json` `replace: {"phpmailer/phpmailer": "*"}` claims compatibility with every upstream PHPMailer version including future majors. If you want to act as a drop-in for the upstream package, constrain the replacement to the supported range (`^7.0` or `~7.0.2`) rather than `*` — otherwise Composer will silently satisfy `^6` or `^8` requirements from other deps with this fork even though the API may not match.
- **[gotcha]** Reading inline review comments by username pattern via `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/<pr>/comments --jq '.[] | select(.user.login | test("chatgpt|codex"; "i"))'` returns 404 for PRs that have ZERO inline review comments (e.g. only top-level review comments or no reviews at all). Don't treat the 404 as a fatal error — skip the PR and continue. Use `gh api .../pulls/<pr>/reviews` if you need the top-level review summaries instead.
- **[pattern]** To bulk-react `+1` to a list of GitHub review comments, POST to `repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/comments/<comment_id>/reactions` with `-f content="+1"`. The comment ID is the same one returned by `gh api .../pulls/<pr>/comments --jq '.[].id'` — works for any commenter (codex, chatgpt-codex-connector, humans, etc.). Successful response includes `"content":"+1"` in the body; use that as a grep check rather than relying on HTTP status.
- **[gotcha]** Webman's built-in `Request::getRealIp(false)` is NOT safe for production — it trusts `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Real-IP` / `Client-IP` regardless of the TCP source, so any internet client can spoof its identity. `getRealIp(true)` is also too coarse (it only trusts intranet remotes). For anything that emits a client IP downstream (e.g. PROXY-protocol headers, audit logs), use `app\Support\TrustedProxyResolver` which gates header trust on a configured `mail.trusted_proxies` CIDR list, walks the X-Forwarded-For chain right-to-left to identify the first untrusted hop, and falls back to `getRemoteIp()` when the source isn't in the trusted set. Same goes for ports — use `resolvePort()` instead of bare `getRemotePort()` so `X-Forwarded-Port` only gets honored from trusted proxies.
- **[gotcha]** `WorkermanConnectionTransport` guards `write/readLine` with an in-fiber check that throws when called outside a fiber. This means pool `release()` (internally `reset()` + stash) and explicit `$smtp->quit(true)` MUST happen INSIDE the same `FiberRunner::run()` closure that did the send — not after it returns. Calling them post-Fiber also re-enters a fresh private Revolt loop that doesn't track the long-lived `AsyncTcpConnection` watchers, causing hangs. Pattern in `app/controller/Mail.php::rawsend()`: do MAIL/RCPT/DATA, then either `pool->release()` or `quit(true)` on the same fiber, then return only a plain array of results to the outer scope. ALSO: every connect-failure error path inside the fiber (smtpConnect()=false, PROXY-fallback failure, etc.) must call `quit()`-if-connected-else-`close()` before returning the error array, otherwise a half-opened SMTP (TCP up, AUTH failed) leaks until end of request. Use a single in-fiber `$teardownAndError` closure to route all five error returns through.
- **[gotcha]** Webman/Workerman renames its forked processes after start: the master shows as `WorkerMan: master process` and children as `WorkerMan: worker process  webman http://0.0.0.0:8787`. `pkill -f "php start.php"` ONLY kills the original launcher, NOT the daemonized workers — they keep holding port 8787, so the next `php start.php start` boots and immediately dies with `stream_socket_server(): Unable to connect to tcp://0.0.0.0:8787 (Address already in use)`. To actually free the port: `pkill -9 -f "WorkerMan"` (catches both master and workers), then `ss -ltn | grep :8787` to confirm the port is free before retrying. The Bash tool will appear to hang on the boot attempt even though the real error is the port collision in the boot log.

# CLAUDE.md

Source: https://github.com/interserver/mailbaby-mail-api/blob/master/CLAUDE.md

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

MailBaby Mail API is a REST-based email service API built with **PHP + Webman framework** (which uses Workerman as the underlying async event loop). It handles email sending, routing rules, block lists, statistics, and account management for the Mail.Baby platform.

## Common Commands

**Start the server:**
```bash
php start.php
```

**CLI user/config management (via webman console):**
```bash
php webman user:add <username> <password>
php webman user:list
php webman user:show <username>
php webman user:pass <username> <new_password>
php webman user:remove <username>
php webman config:sql
```

**API spec management:**
```bash
./update-spec.sh           # Rebuild public/spec/openapi.{json,yaml}
./update-ui.sh             # Refresh documentation viewer HTML files
./openapi-generator-cli.sh # Regenerate language client libraries
```

**Lint the OpenAPI spec:**
```bash
# Uses .spectral.yaml config
npx @stoplight/spectral-cli lint public/spec/openapi.yaml
```

**Run PHPUnit tests:**
```bash
php vendor/bin/phpunit
```

**Manual API testing:**
```bash
test/manual/send_simple.sh
test/manual/send_adv_attachment.sh
```

## Architecture

### Request Flow
```
HTTP Request
  → CORS middleware (webman/cors plugin)
  → AuthCheck middleware (validates X-API-KEY header against account_security table)
  → Router (config/route.php)
  → Controller
  → Illuminate Database (MySQL / MongoDB)
  → JSON response
```

### Key Files
| Path | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `config/route.php` | All API endpoint definitions |
| `config/database.php` | Multi-database connection configs |
| `config/server.php` | HTTP server (port 8787, 16 workers, 10MB max packet, `event_loop` pinned to `Workerman\Events\Fiber`) |
| `config/mail.php` | SMTP relay config (`MAIL_RELAY_HOST`, `MAIL_RELAY_PORT`, `MAIL_PROXY_PROTOCOL_ENABLED`, `MAIL_API_SERVER_IP`, `MAIL_SMTP_TIMEOUT`, `MAIL_SMTP_DEBUG`, `MAIL_TRUSTED_PROXIES`) |
| `config/bootstrap.php` | Webman bootstrap registrations (session + `app/bootstrap/SmtpPoolBootstrap.php`) |
| `app/middleware/AuthCheck.php` | API key validation |
| `app/controller/Mail.php` | Core email send logic (send, rawsend, advsend, log, view) |
| `app/controller/Mail/Rules.php` | Email routing rule CRUD |
| `app/controller/Mail/Stats.php` | Usage/billing stats from ZoneMTA DB |
| `app/controller/Mail/Blocks.php` | Blocklist management |
| `app/Mail/ProxySMTP.php` | PHPMailer `SMTP` subclass that injects a PROXY Protocol v1 header so ZoneMTA sees the real client IP |
| `app/Support/TrustedProxyResolver.php` | Trusted-proxy gate for client IP/port resolution (walks `X-Forwarded-For` only when the TCP peer is in `mail.trusted_proxies`) |
| `app/bootstrap/SmtpPoolBootstrap.php` | `Webman\Bootstrap` that drains the SMTP pool on `onWorkerStop` |
| `app/controller/Mcp.php` | MCP server endpoint + agent-readiness well-known routes |
| `app/Mcp/OpenApiParser.php` | Parses `public/spec/openapi.yaml` into MCP tool definitions (cached under `runtime/mcp/cache/`) |
| `app/Mcp/McpServerFactory.php` | Builds the MCP server instance from parsed tools |
| `app/Mcp/Bridge.php` | Dispatches MCP tool calls back into Webman controllers |
| `app/Mcp/Skills/` | Agent Skills 0.2.0 SKILL.md files served via `/.well-known/agent-skills/` |
| `app/controller/BaseController.php` | `jsonResponse()` / `jsonErrorResponse()` helpers |
| `app/command/` | CLI commands registered with webman console |
| `public/spec/openapi.yaml` | Canonical OpenAPI 3.0 spec (source of truth) |
| `public/webmcp.js` | WebMCP browser-side manifest helper |
| `phpunit.xml.dist` | PHPUnit config — points at `test/` (singular), bootstrap `test/bootstrap.php` |

### Multi-Database Design
The service deliberately queries multiple databases for different concerns:
- **Primary MySQL** (`DB_*` env vars) — customer accounts, mail orders, routing rules, blocks
- **ZoneMTA MySQL** (`ZONEMTA_*`) — email send/receive statistics and message tracking
- **Rspamd MySQL** (`RSPAMD_*`) — spam scores and malware detection results
- **MongoDB** (`MONGO_*`) — user account data (supplementary)
- **Redis** — session storage and caching

### Authentication
All `/mail/*` routes require an `X-API-KEY` header. The middleware resolves it to an account via the `account_security` table on the primary MySQL connection.

### OpenAPI Spec
`public/spec/openapi.yaml` is the canonical spec. The JSON version at `public/spec/openapi.json` is generated from it. Documentation UIs (Swagger UI, ReDoc, RapiDoc, Stoplight Elements, OpenAPI Explorer) all serve from `public/`.

### MCP Server
The MCP (Model Context Protocol) server is mounted at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) and exposes the OpenAPI spec as MCP tools. Agent-readiness discovery endpoints are served from `app/controller/Mcp.php`: `/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json` (canonical), `/.well-known/mcp.json`, `/.well-known/mcp`, `/.well-known/mcp/server.json` (legacy aliases), `/.well-known/webmcp{,.json}`, `/.well-known/agent-skills/index.json`, `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`, and `/.well-known/api-catalog`. Public assets `public/llms.txt`, `public/robots.txt`, and `public/sitemap.xml` complement the discovery surface.

### Response Pattern
Controllers use helpers from `BaseController`:
- `$this->jsonResponse($data)` — 200 success
- `$this->jsonErrorResponse($message, $code)` — error responses

### Environment
Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and configure the database connection strings before starting. Mail relay settings (`MAIL_RELAY_HOST`, `MAIL_RELAY_PORT`, `MAIL_PROXY_PROTOCOL_ENABLED`, `MAIL_API_SERVER_IP`, `MAIL_SMTP_TIMEOUT`, `MAIL_SMTP_DEBUG`, `MAIL_TRUSTED_PROXIES`) are read by `config/mail.php` and drive `app/Mail/ProxySMTP.php` and `app/Support/TrustedProxyResolver.php`. `MAIL_TRUSTED_PROXIES` is a comma-separated CIDR list (e.g. `10.0.0.0/8,127.0.0.1/32`) of upstream proxies whose `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Port` headers may be trusted. The server listens on `0.0.0.0:8787` with 16 worker processes.

<!-- caliber:managed:pre-commit -->
## Before Committing

**IMPORTANT:** Before every git commit, you MUST ensure Caliber syncs agent configs with the latest code changes.

First, check if the pre-commit hook is already installed:
```bash
grep -q "caliber" .git/hooks/pre-commit 2>/dev/null && echo "hook-active" || echo "no-hook"
```

- If **hook-active**: the hook handles sync automatically — just commit normally. Tell the user: "Caliber will sync your agent configs automatically via the pre-commit hook."
- If **no-hook**: run Caliber manually before committing:
  1. Tell the user: "Caliber: Syncing agent configs with your latest changes..."
  2. Run: `caliber refresh && git add CALIBER_LEARNINGS.md CLAUDE.md .claude/ 2>/dev/null`
  3. After it completes, briefly tell the user what Caliber updated. Then proceed with the commit.

**Valid `caliber refresh` options:** `--quiet` (suppress output) and `--dry-run` (preview without writing). Do not pass any other flags — options like `--auto-approve`, `--debug`, or `--force` do not exist and will cause errors.

**`caliber config`** takes no flags — it runs an interactive provider setup. Do not pass `--provider`, `--api-key`, or `--endpoint`.

If `caliber` is not found, tell the user: "This project uses Caliber for agent config sync. Run /setup-caliber to get set up."
<!-- /caliber:managed:pre-commit -->

<!-- caliber:managed:model-config -->
## Model Configuration

Recommended default: `claude-sonnet-4-6` with high effort (stronger reasoning; higher cost and latency than smaller models).
Smaller/faster models trade quality for speed and cost — pick what fits the task.
Pin your choice (`/model` in Claude Code, or `CALIBER_MODEL` when using Caliber with an API provider) so upstream default changes do not silently change behavior.

<!-- /caliber:managed:model-config -->

<!-- caliber:managed:sync -->
## Context Sync

This project uses [Caliber](https://github.com/caliber-ai-org/ai-setup) to keep AI agent configs in sync across Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and Codex.
Configs update automatically before each commit via `caliber refresh`.
If the pre-commit hook is not set up, run `/setup-caliber` to configure everything automatically.
<!-- /caliber:managed:sync -->

# Security Update Workflow

Source: https://github.com/interserver/mailbaby-mail-api/blob/master/SECURITY_UPDATES.md

# Security Update Workflow

This project updates generated clients in `mailbaby-api-samples` across multiple language ecosystems.

## 1) Install security tooling

Run on Ubuntu/Debian:

```bash
./install-security-tools.sh
```

The installer sets up tooling used by `update-samples-security.sh`, including:

- Java/Maven: `mvn`, OWASP dependency-check plugin
- Node: `npm`, `audit-ci`, `npm-check-updates`
- PHP: `composer`
- Python: `pip-audit`, `safety`
- Ruby: `bundler-audit`
- Go: `govulncheck`
- Rust: `cargo-audit`
- .NET: `dotnet`, `dotnet-outdated`
- Dart: `dart pub`
- Elixir: `mix hex.audit`
- Swift: `swift package`
- R: `Rscript`

## 2) Run security updates

```bash
./update-samples-security.sh /home/sites/mailbaby-mail-api/mailbaby-api-samples
```

Environment variables:

- `SECURITY_UPDATE_MODE=update` (default): updates dependencies where possible and runs checks.
- `SECURITY_UPDATE_MODE=check`: audit/check only, no dependency upgrades.

Example check-only run:

```bash
SECURITY_UPDATE_MODE=check ./update-samples-security.sh /home/sites/mailbaby-mail-api/mailbaby-api-samples
```

## Notes

- The script is resilient: one ecosystem failure does not stop the whole run.
- Missing tools are skipped with a clear log message.
- Temporary dependency directories are cleaned when practical (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `target`).
